description: Backend redesign: new SemanticClassMapper, upgraded nested SearchIntent schema, updated search/response services, and slim app.py wiring with _last_debug_result. Covers plan steps 1–5.
steps: Step 1 — Create class_mapper.py at the project root (c:\Users\praan\Desktop\vista_platform\class_mapper.py). Define SYNONYM_MAP dict. Implement SemanticClassMapper with two static methods: resolve(concept, available_classes) and describe_unsupported(attributes). resolve() normalizes concept to lowercase, checks exact match in available_classes, falls back to SYNONYM_MAP, returns only classes present in available_classes. describe_unsupported() returns the subset of attributes that are colors, clothing references, or size modifiers the detector cannot verify.

Step 2 — Update query_parser.py. Replace the flat SearchIntent @dataclass (which had target_object, attributes, related_object, relation, action, motion, event, time_window_seconds, raw_query) with four new dataclasses: TargetEntity(type, attributes, description), RelatedEntity(type, attributes), Relation(type), SearchIntent(target, related_entities, relations, action, temporal_constraint, original_query, unsupported_attributes). Do NOT use slots=True on these classes. Update _fallback_intent() to populate the new nested fields. Update _validate_intent() to parse the new nested JSON keys (target dict, related_entities list, relations list, unsupported_attributes list, temporal_constraint, original_query). Update _intent_to_dict() to return the nested structure. Update build_parser_prompt() to use the new schema example with nested target/related_entities/relations/unsupported_attributes, YOLO vocabulary list, and synonym-mapping rules (automobile→car, vehicle→car/truck/bus/motorcycle/bicycle, pedestrian/human→person, etc.).

Step 3 — Update response_service.py. In _build_response_prompt(), access intent.target.type (not intent.target_object), intent.related_entities[0].type if non-empty (not intent.related_object), intent.relations[0].type if non-empty (not intent.relation), intent.temporal_constraint (not intent.time_window_seconds), intent.original_query (not intent.raw_query), intent.unsupported_attributes. Update the system prompt in generate_response() to explicitly say: do not show track IDs or confidence numbers in the answer; if unsupported_attributes is non-empty, acknowledge those attributes could not be visually verified. Update _mock_response() to produce a clean human-friendly string without track ID or frame number.

Step 4 — Update search_service.py. Add available_classes: set[str] | None = None parameter to VisualSearchEngine.__init__(). Import SemanticClassMapper from class_mapper. Replace self.target_object string with self.target_classes list (resolved via SemanticClassMapper.resolve, with fallback to normalized raw string if mapper returns empty). Replace self.related_object string with self.related_classes list (same pattern). Store self.unsupported_attributes from intent.unsupported_attributes. Update _is_target() to check if normalized record.object_class matches any class in self.target_classes. Update _is_related() same way for self.related_classes. In finalize(), use self.target_classes[0] where the old code used self.target_object string, and self.related_classes[0] where it used self.related_object. Populate the notes list if self.unsupported_attributes is non-empty.

Step 5 — Update app.py. Add _last_debug_result: dict | None = None at module level. Add available_classes = set(model.names.values()) in process_video(), pass it to VisualSearchEngine(..., available_classes=available_classes). Update the VisualSearchEngine guard condition to check intent.target.type / intent.related_entities / intent.action (new schema). Import _intent_to_dict from query_parser and use it for the 'intent' key in the result dict. In the /process route handler, after a successful call to process_video(), assign global _last_debug_result = result. Change the render_home() call to pass only: answer_text=result.get('assistant_message',''), answer_ok=result.get('assistant_ok',False), matched_image=result['images'][0] if result.get('images') else None, query=query, error=None. Update render_home() signature to accept (answer_text, answer_ok, matched_image, query, error) and pass only those 5 to render_template('index.html', ...). Update the GET / route's render_home call to pass all-None/False/empty. Add a /debug GET route that calls render_template('debug.html', result=_last_debug_result, runtime_status=model_status()).

findings: render_home() signature: render_home(answer_text: str|None, answer_ok: bool, matched_image: dict|None, query: str, error: str|None). Template variables passed to index.html: answer_text, answer_ok, matched_image, query, error. Template variables passed to debug.html: result (full _last_debug_result dict or None), runtime_status (dict from model_status()). matched_image is result['images'][0] (dict with keys: filename, frame_no, class_name, confidence, track_id) or None. The project uses .venv at project root — all python commands must use .venv/Scripts/python.exe. debug.html is a minimal but functional standalone template (no inheritance). index.html still uses old render_home fields (result, error, query, runtime_status) — FEAT-002 must rewrite it to use the new 5-param signature. Dataclasses: TargetEntity, RelatedEntity, Relation, SearchIntent all use plain @dataclass (no slots=True). _intent_to_dict() is importable from query_parser.
